mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0 for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, signaling economic weakness that drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production below 95.0 (INDPRO < 95.0) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0, or Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 500.0 thousand units (HOUST < 500.0) indicates a weak housing market that depresses consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 500.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220.0) triggers central bank tightening expectations that increase discount rates and reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220.0, or Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS growth) indicates improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is rising, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in retail sales (RSAFS) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate broad economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances when both RSAFS and GDPC1 decline, or interaction Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
